speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have some concerning skin lesions; to begin our assessment, can you describe their appearance, including their color, shape, and whether they are changing in size or texture?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the history; given your heavy smoking history and the specific description of non-healing, crusty lesions on both the penis and a finger, are these lesions currently bleeding, ulcerated, or painful? Also, have you noticed any new lumps in your groin or armpit?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Non-healing, crusty, red lesions on the penile shaft and left middle finger. I also have Lesions are painless, History of unsuccessful treatment for syphilis and eczema.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (SCC) of the penis and digit.

The clinical picture of non-healing, painless, crusty lesions in a heavy smoker with a history of failed treatment for syphilis and eczema is highly suggestive of invasive squamous cell carcinoma. I recommend a biopsy of the penile and digital lesions immediately to confirm the diagnosis and determine the stage.
